newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania to try ailing alleged war criminal.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania to try ailing alleged war criminal.

text.p: VILNIUS, June 24 (Vilnius) - Lithuanian prosecutors, accused of being slow to try Nazi war criminals, on Tuesday said they intend to try a man alleged to have handed over scores of Jews to death squads in World War Two.

But the prosecutor's office said the poor health of 90-year-old Aleksandras Lileikis, head of the Vilnius security police in Nazi-occupied Lithuania, meant any further action had to be delayed for three months.
Nazi-hunters have criticised Lithuania for apparent foot-dragging over Lileikis and other alleged war criminals who were stripped of U.S. citizenship and returned to Lithuania.
"There is a decision to put Aleksandras Lileikis on trial for the genocide of inhabitants of Lithuania," the prosecutor's office said in a statement.
But it said that due to Lileikis' ill health, questioning was possible only in three months and with the permission of a medical commission.

Lileikis denies he helped to murder Jews during the Holocaust but his U.S. citizenship was revoked last year on the grounds that he had concealed his wartime activities. He returned to Lithuania last June.
Historians say that 94 percent of Lithuania's flourishing pre-war Jewish population of 220,000 was wiped out during the war by Nazis and their local helpers.
In March, Israel's Knesset urged Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas to ensure that Lileikis be brought to trial.
Efraim Zhuroff, head of the Simon Wiesenthal Centre in Jerusalem, cautiously welcomed the news of the intention to prosecute Lileikis.
"It remains to be seen whether Liliekis' advanced age may prevent justice from being achieved," he told Reuters.
"At the same time, it is important to remember that there are numerous other war criminals who have returned to Lithuania and have not yet been questioned let alone indicted," he added.
